subject: Acme: elevated 5xx/429 spikes — auth/gateway misreporting
messages:
From: Danielle Park <danielle.park@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Ops <ops@acme.com>, Antonio Gomez <antonio.gomez@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429s impacting production — need immediate help

Marissa —

We started seeing a large uptick in 5xx and 429 responses to our production calls around 16:30 UTC (09:30 PT). Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~6% and a few customer-facing requests timed out repeatedly. Our retry logic amplified traffic which caused throughput to spike briefly, then throttles kicked in.

Attached are a small sample of traces and the gateway logs we captured (acme_5xx_sample_traces.zip). We're seeing repeated error bodies that look like generic 5xx but with hints of auth failures — e.g. "token invalid" in one trace and "gateway: upstream timeout" in others.

This is affecting two high-traffic endpoints. Can you please escalate to infra and confirm whether this is on Redwood's side (gateway/token validation) or if it's something on our end (clock skew, token generation)? We need a short window of time when you can join a call.

-Danielle
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <danielle.park@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s impacting production — need immediate help

Thanks Danielle —

Sorry you're seeing this. I'm escalating and looping in infra (Rishi) and incident lead (Evelyn). Initial ask: can you share the timestamped request ids (X-Req-Id) and the exact error payloads (we saw the ZIP — thank you)? If you can include the raw JWT from any failing requests (we can sanitize) that will help us rule out signature/clock issues quickly.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Rishi will look at gateway metrics and auth service logs for token validation spikes.
- We'll check token validation latency and whether the gateway is misclassifying auth errors as 5xx/429.
- If retry storms look likely, we'll propose a short temporary rate-limiter to reduce blast radius.

Can we do a 30-min bridge at 10:00 PT? I'll send a calendar invite.

—Marissa
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Danielle Park <danielle.park@acme.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s impacting production — need immediate help

On it. Quick summary of what I'm pulling now: gateway logs, auth-service (JWT verifier) timelines, rate-limiter telemetry, and pod-level CPU/memory around 16:20–16:45 UTC.

Preliminary notes (very early):
- We see a correlated increase in 502/504 responses reported by the gateway and a separate bump in 429s from the rate limiter.
- A subset of the gateway errors include text like "upstream jwt validation: expired token" but the gateway should be mapping that to 401; we're seeing it bubble as 502 in the logs because the auth-check container times out and returns 502 to the gateway.
- Also checking if there was a clock drift incident in the auth fleet; small skews can cause JWT "exp" checks to fail briefly at scale.

Attaching the initial dumps: jwt_dump_20260302.txt (sanitized), gateway-logs-20260302.csv. I'll correlate request ids next and add trace ids.

-Rishi
Senior Systems Engineer, Infra
Redwood Inference

From: Antonio Gomez <antonio.gomez@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Danielle Park <danielle.park@acme.com>, Acme Ops <ops@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s impacting production — need immediate help

Marissa / Rishi —

We appreciate the quick triage. For context, this incident caused a ~12% error experience for end users on our web checkout for about 8 minutes before our client-side backoff reduced retries. We're flagging this for our executive team; please prioritize clarity on whether this was misclassified auth failures vs. true upstream timeouts. If it's the former, we need a fix and a postmortem in 48 hours.

-Antonio
CTO, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Antonio Gomez <antonio.gomez@acme.com>, Danielle Park <danielle.park@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s impacting production — need immediate help

Antonio —

Understood. Status update: Rishi's analysis shows the following root-candidate chain (high level):
1) A subset of auth-verifier pods experienced transient GC pauses and a concurrent NTP drift on one availability zone, causing JWT verification to intermittently fail with "token expired" for tokens issued just prior to the drift.
2) The auth-check container timed out waiting for the verifier response; due to a bug in the gateway mapping logic, those timeouts were returned as 502/504 instead of 401. That misclassification caused our observability to surface a 5xx spike rather than an auth failure.
3) Client retry logic without jitter amplified incoming request volume; the rate limiter started returning 429s under the increased load, which created the mixed 5xx/429 symptom.

Immediate mitigations we've taken (completed at 16:55 UTC):
- Scaled auth-verifier replicas in the affected AZ and restarted the NTP daemon on those instances.
- Applied a temporary gateway mapping rule to convert auth-check timeouts to 401 within the gateway to avoid masking auth failures as 5xx.
- Deployed a short-lived circuit-breaker at the gateway for the two endpoints to prevent retry storms from escalating.

Next actions (we'll deliver in the follow-up incident report):
- Permanent fix to gateway mapping logic to ensure auth errors are mapped correctly.
- Add NTP monitoring and alerting for auth fleet clock skew.
- Add request-id correlation in the auth path to make root cause faster to detect.
- Draft postmortem and send within 48 hours (target: 2026-03-04T18:00:00Z).

Attached: trace correlation sample and logs we used (acme_5xx_sample_traces.zip). We're preparing a short exec note for your leadership and ours.

—Marissa
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Antonio Gomez <antonio.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 02:03:00 +0000
Subject: Post-incident note and exec summary (draft)

Team / Acme execs —

Draft exec summary (please review and flag edits):
- Impact: A ~8-minute window of increased 5xx/429 responses resulted in ~12% error rate on Acme checkout (customer-visible). No data loss observed.
- Root cause: Combined transient auth-verifier GC/NTP drift caused JWT exp checks to intermittently fail; gateway mapping bug surfaced those as 5xx; client retries created a rate-limiter-driven 429 surge.
- Immediate mitigations: scaled auth-service, NTP restart, temporary gateway 401 mapping, gateway circuit-breaker.
- Next steps: permanent gateway mapping fix; NTP monitoring and runbook; add explicit auth error metrics and request-id correlation; postmortem by 2026-03-04.

I'll finalize the timeline and technical appendix (trace ids, metrics) and publish the postmortem publicly to your team. Thanks to Rishi and Connor for the rapid mitigations and to Marissa for running the customer comms.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Incidents & Reliability
Redwood Inference
